label: Further Techniques
notes: Open the chapter as the technical upgrade layer. After curves and surfaces vocabulary, this chapter develops spectral sequences, fixed-point and Lefschetz arguments, blowups along subvarieties, and refined intersection theory. The deck follows printed pages 364 through 468. These are tools that the surface chapter and onward will use repeatedly.

label: Spectral Sequences
notes: Introduce spectral sequences. A spectral sequence is a sequence of differential bigraded objects converging to a cohomology of interest. The Leray spectral sequence for a fibration packages how cohomology of fibers builds up to cohomology of the total space. It is the main computational engine in this chapter.

label: Lefschetz Fixed Point
notes: Present the Lefschetz fixed-point formula. The alternating sum of traces on cohomology equals the count of fixed points weighted by local indices. On algebraic varieties this becomes a powerful enumerative tool, especially combined with the Lefschetz hyperplane theorem for restriction of cohomology to ample divisors.

label: Blowups
notes: Cover blowups along smooth subvarieties. The blowup replaces a smooth subvariety by its projectivized normal bundle. Cohomology of the blowup splits cleanly. The exceptional divisor records the geometry of the subvariety. This is the standard surgery tool when working with rational maps and resolutions.

label: Intersection Theory
notes: Refine intersection theory. On smooth projective varieties, intersection of cycles is well-defined in the Chow ring; for complex varieties this agrees with cup product in cohomology. The chapter introduces moving lemmas, excess intersection formulas, and the projection formula that drive computations.

label: Recap
notes: Close by collecting the techniques. Spectral sequences for fibrations, Lefschetz fixed-point and hyperplane arguments, blowup splittings, and intersection-theoretic refinements. These are the technical instruments used in the surface chapter that follows and in the more advanced computational chapters.
